catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andre-jean-cu:
Andre-Jean Cuoq, a philologist, was born at Le Puy in France in 1821 and died at Oka, near Montreal, in 1898. He entered the Company of Saint-Sulpice in 1844 and was sent to Canada two years later. In 1847 he took charge of the mission at Lac des Deux-Montagnes. Eager to serve well, he soon mastered the Iroquois and Algonquin dialects.

His many works, all published at Montreal, won him entry to scientific societies in Europe and America. They include a book of seven nations in 1861 and a reply to Renan in 1864. Later came studies of savage languages in 1866 and of the peoples Cartier met in 1869. His Iroquois lexicon of 1882, Algonquin lexicon of 1886, and Algonquin grammar of 1891 remain his chief legacy, beside works for christianizing the Indians.

Comedian Doug Stanhope joins Joe Rogan to recount his DMT experience in a segment from the show. Stanhope is a comic known for bleak, fearless sets. His drug tales are a staple of his act and of his talks with Rogan.

Stanhope tells the trip in his own rough, funny words, from the blast-off to the beings he swears he met. Rogan, a famed fan of the drug, trades notes with him. The segment is short, raw, and very much for grown ears. Listeners get a comic's take on the strongest trip there is. The library holds the file as an archive record.
